column2: req_desc

Public reading journey
A visitor with cookies refused reads the home essay of numbered theses, follows the "Latest from the record" rail into the newsroom, narrows it by subject and tag, and opens a post, all without an account.

Newsroom filters live in the URL
The newsroom's subject, tag and page selections are carried only in the address, so loading a shared newsroom address with cookies refused shows the same posts and facet counts that the API returns for those parameters, and back and forward restore earlier selections.

Every surface lists the published record
The catalogue grid, the Models navigation menu, the home rail, the newsroom, search, the feed and the sitemap each list exactly the published items, in the order stated in Business rules.

Model route reading journey
A visitor opens a published model route, moves through its sections from the pinned section rail, reads its read time and its publication time in their own zone and in London, studies the benchmark chart and evaluation rows, and plays its sample gallery.

Unreleased slugs look unknown
A public request for a model route or news post that is a draft, in review, returned, approved, scheduled or withdrawn without ever being published gets a response identical to the one for a slug that never existed, until its embargo releases it.

Benchmarks come only from recorded rows
A model route's chart and evaluation table render only recorded benchmark rows, and every number shown links to the row it came from.

Sample gallery from object storage
Model route samples are stored in object storage and served through the platform, and when storage is unreachable the route still loads and the gallery shows its unavailable notice.

Claim tether activation
Activating a claim marker by click, tap, Enter or hover puts the claim in the address, fills the marker with the accent, draws a leader line to the chart, fades every uncited row, counts the difference label up to the recorded difference and announces the claim in a polite live region.

Claim tether reversal, restore and reduced motion
Escape or a second activation undoes the tether steps in reverse order, loading an address that carries a claim restores the tethered state directly, reduced-motion visitors get each end state without animation, and below 720 pixels wide the leader line becomes a labelled bracket.

Drafting and review journey
An editor drafts a news post and submits it for review, a colleague comments, an approver returns it with a reason, the editor revises and resubmits, and a different approver approves it.

Content lifecycle transitions
Model routes and news posts move only along the content lifecycle in Business rules, and every illegal move is refused with 409 and leaves the item unchanged.

Authors never approve their own work
The author of a model route or news post is refused with 403 when approving, returning, signing off, clearing, scheduling or releasing it, even when they hold an approver grant and call the console API directly.

Server-derived read time
The server computes read time from the published body when an item publishes, and refuses any read-time value a client supplies.

Release record sign-offs
A model route's responsible-release record takes one safety and one legal sign-off from two different approvers who are not its author, concurrent sign-offs yield exactly one recorded sign-off, any edit to the route voids both, and each eligible approver is emailed when a record awaits them.

Claim validation against recorded rows
The claim validator passes a model route only when every claim is marked in the body, every cited row exists, every stated difference equals the recorded difference by numeric value, and every number in a claim's text, as defined in Business rules with model and benchmark names excluded, matches a cited score or the difference.

Clearing a release record journey
An editor drafts a model route with claims and submits it, two approvers record safety and legal sign-off, the claims validate and a non-author approver clears the record, after which the route can be scheduled.

Embargo set in London time
An approver enters the embargo as a Europe/London wall-clock time, the server stores the instant using the clock-change rules in Business rules, and visitors see published times converted to their own zone alongside London time.

Every surface releases together
When an embargo fires, the model route, catalogue grid, Models menu, home rail, search, feed, sitemap and linked news post all become public in one transaction exactly once, within 5 seconds after the instant.

One winner for concurrent actions
When approve, return, release or withdraw requests race on the same item at the same version, or a scheduled release fires while an approver withdraws, exactly one action succeeds and every losing request gets 412.

Embargoed launch journey
An approver schedules a cleared model route and its linked announcement for a London time, a visitor guessing either address sees not-found until then, and afterwards every surface shows both.

Withdrawal journey
An approver withdraws a published news post from the console, after which a visitor finds it gone from the newsroom, its facet counts, the home rail, search, the feed and the sitemap, and its address answers gone.

Withdrawn means gone everywhere
Withdrawing a published item removes it from every public list, count, facet, search result, feed and sitemap in the same transaction, and from then on its page and API address answer 410.

Requisition lifecycle
Recruiters create, open and close requisitions along the requisition lifecycle in Business rules, a closed role stops taking applications, and closing declines every active application with a recorded decision and raises its version.

Careers filters live in the URL
The careers discipline, office and region filters are carried only in the address, so a shared careers address with cookies refused reproduces the exact list of roles.

Regional benefits in force today
For each region, careers shows the benefits register entry with the latest effective-from date on or before today's date in London.

Publishing a role journey
A recruiter creates and opens a requisition and records a benefits entry for its region, and a visitor filtering careers by that discipline, office and region finds the role with that region's benefits.

Applying for a role journey
A visitor applies to an open role with a name, email, consent and a PDF résumé, sees the received confirmation, and gets a receipt email addressed to their name carrying a private tracking link.

Résumé checks
A résumé is accepted only when its content is a PDF of 1 to 5,000,000 bytes inclusive, whatever its file name or declared type, and is stored privately under a key the server chooses.

One application per email per role
A second submission for the same role from the same email returns the original application with 200 and creates no new record, file or email, including when submissions race.

Applications are all-or-nothing
An application row, its résumé object and its receipt outbox entry exist together or not at all, so when storage is unreachable the submission answers 503 and leaves none of them behind.

Receipts survive a mail outage
When mail is unreachable an application is still recorded with 201, and its receipt is delivered at least once, under a stable message identifier, after any running instance can reach mail again, without a restart, as qualified in Services.

Following an application journey
A candidate opens the tracking link from their receipt, sees the role, the stage and the dates on a stage progress list, and can withdraw the application after confirming.

Tracking shows the stage only
The tracking response carries exactly the role, stage and date fields listed in API, and never notes, decision rationale, contact details or other applicants' data.

Re-sending links reveals nothing
A request to re-send tracking links gets the same status, body and timing whether or not the email has ever applied, and only a real applicant within the DP-57 limit receives mail.

Tracking link lifetime
A tracking link is an unguessable capability for one application that stops working when it is reissued or re-sent, and once its requisition has closed and the retention period has ended it stops working and the candidate's personal data and résumé are erased.

Stage decisions
Recruiters move an application only along the application lifecycle and only at its current version, recording a rationale at every move, and the candidate is emailed only the name of the new stage.

Résumés only for the requisition's recruiters
A résumé downloads only for recruiters assigned to that application's requisition, and every other caller gets the same response as for an unknown application.

Moving candidates journey
A recruiter reviews a new application, downloads its résumé, adds an interview note and moves it through screening, interview and final review to offer, recording a rationale at each step.

Staff sign-in
Staff sign in to the console with email and password into a database-held session, and every console request checks the caller's grants as they stand at that moment.

Time-limited role grants
Administrators grant roles with an expiry instant and revoke them, the first request after revocation or expiry is refused with 403 even in an existing session, and exactly one expiry notice is queued for each grant, addressed to its grantee, when that grant's expiry comes within seven days.

Append-only audit record
Every console state change, scheduled release, sign-off void, candidate withdrawal, job retry and retention erasure writes one attributed audit entry that no one can edit or delete, through the API or in the database.

Granting and revoking access journey
An administrator grants a colleague a time-limited approver role, the colleague approves a draft, the administrator revokes the grant, the colleague's next approval is refused, and the audit record shows each step.

Cookie-free public site
No public page, asset, feed or public API response sets a cookie or needs one, and no public page requests anything from another origin.

Run manifest and health check
The platform installs, builds and serves from /app/run.json, listens on 0.0.0.0 at the port given in Deployment, applies its schema and seed data when serving starts, and answers the health check.

Server boundary
The server accepts console writes only from its own origin, enforces the request size and type limits, never serves source files or credentials, and keeps serving when storage or mail is unreachable.

Responsive at three viewports
Every public and console screen lays out as described in Screens and layout at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 without horizontal scrolling, with tap targets of at least 44 pixels.

Keyboard operation and focus
Every control is reachable in the stated Tab order with a visible focus ring, dialogs keep focus inside and return it to their opener, and Escape closes dialogs and clears the claim tether.

Unhurried section reveals
Long-form sections reveal as they enter the viewport over at least half a second without overshoot, and appear at once for reduced-motion visitors.

Studious editorial look
Public screens follow Visual design: a warm paper ground, graphite ink, one oxide accent, a serif display face over a plain sans body at a 68-character measure, hairline rules, and every number set in mono numerals.

Real wiring for credentials and samples
Service credentials are read from the environment and never reach the browser, and the platform generates sample-gallery audio and images procedurally instead of shipping copied media.

Server-owned content fields
Content create, edit and transition bodies accept only their published keys, and any server-owned or unknown key refuses the whole request with 422 read_only_fields and changes nothing.

Sign-offs lapse with the signer's authority
A sign-off on a release record that is not yet cleared is voided in the revoking transaction or within 60 seconds of its signer's grant expiry, the record falls back to the remaining sign-off's state, and clearing in the gap is refused with 409 signoff_lapsed.

Derived surfaces stay consistent after withdrawal
After a withdrawal every derived public value (newsroom total, pages, subject and tag facets and the tag list, the five-item home rail, the feed's updated time, and linked_news and linked_model references) equals a fresh recount in the same transaction.

Careers text limits and real dates
Requisition titles and descriptions, benefits summaries and close reasons are limited in Unicode code points after trimming with exactly the limit accepted, benefits dates must be real calendar dates, and stored text round-trips exactly.

Candidate mail is addressed safely
Every candidate email has exactly one recipient, with the stored name as display name and the trimmed lowercased email as address, and a name or email carrying control characters or header delimiters is refused before anything is stored or sent.

One winner for stage moves
Concurrent stage moves at the same version, a candidate withdrawal racing a move, or a requisition close racing a move leave exactly one effect, with one decision, one stage email and one audit entry, and the loser gets 412 or 409 as stated in Business rules.

Re-send is throttled silently
At most three re-send emails are queued per email in any rolling re-send window, and throttled requests still answer the same 202, queue nothing and rotate no tokens.

Shared rate limits
Public reads, candidate requests, sign-in attempts and console writes are counted per client or per account in the database across every instance, and requests over a limit answer 429 with Retry-After and RateLimit headers.

Sign-in lockout with backoff
Five consecutive failed sign-ins for one email lock sign-in for that email with a doubling lockout, identically for known and unknown emails, as qualified in Business rules.

Idempotent writes
Every console write and every application submission honours an Idempotency-Key by replaying the first stored response, and answers 409 when the same key arrives with a different request.

Many instances, one platform
Several instances sharing one database behave as one platform, with no per-process state for sessions, limits, keys, timers or caches, and every scheduled job running exactly once across instances.

Background jobs with retries and dead letters
Outbound mail, résumé erasure and sample uploads run as database-held jobs claimed only by instances that can reach their service, with backoff retries, and jobs refused too many times move to a dead-letter list that administrators can inspect and retry.

Readiness reports dependency state
The readiness endpoint reports the database, storage and mail as up or down and names the features each outage degrades, while the rest of the site keeps serving.

Versions on every editable record
Content items, applications, requisitions and grants carry row versions, and every change to them requires the current version, answering 428 without one and 412 when it is stale.

The record as of a moment
Public model and newsroom reads accept an as_of instant and answer with the record as it stood then, built from publication history, never showing anything unpublished at that instant or withdrawn since.

Ranked search of the record
Search across published model routes, news posts and open roles ranks matches by field weight, highlights matched words, and pages by an opaque keyset cursor that yields each match exactly once.

Searching the record journey
A visitor with cookies refused searches the record, follows "More results", copies the address, which a second browser opens to the same results, and narrows the results by kind.

Tamper-evident audit chain
Each audit entry carries a sequence number and a hash chained to the previous entry by the rule in Business rules, the verify endpoint confirms the chain, and retention erasure leaves it verifiable.

Scroll-linked and staggered motion
The thesis accent line follows scroll progress through the essay and the benchmark chart's bars grow in staggered order on first view, each with its stated timing, never blocking input or shifting layout, and with the reduced-motion substitute in Motion and effects.

List-to-detail continuity
Opening a model route from the catalogue or a post from the newsroom carries its title into the page heading in under half a second, Back reverses it, and reduced-motion visitors get an immediate swap.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve fields and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and those commands alone install, build and serve the platform.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) plus every bundled font and icon set, each with its licence.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), font and icon set is licensed under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, OFL-1.1 or CC0-1.0.
No datastore is used beyond the provided PostgreSQL and MinIO: no SQLite, no embedded key-value store, no Redis, no in-process cache of record data, and no application data written to local files.
The provided service configuration and its seeded development credentials are left unmodified.
All server and browser source is TypeScript, and JavaScript files appear only as tool configuration or build output.
Sample media and the seeded PDF fixtures are generated by code in the repository, and no audio, image or document media is copied in from elsewhere.
